summary: This bill directs the heads of the SBA, IRS, Treasury, Commerce, Agriculture, and Labor departments to launch programs that expand worker-owned cooperatives by reviewing regulations for barriers, facilitating capital access, providing technical assistance for business transitions, and conducting research, while also creating a Labor-led interagency council to develop a federal strategy, coordinate efforts, and report annually, and expanding SBA intermediary lending and CDFI education programs for such cooperatives.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs multiple federal agencies to create new programs, initiatives, research, education, and technical assistance for worker cooperatives. It also establishes a new interagency Council and significantly expands an SBA lending pilot program (increasing authorization from $20M to $60M and extending it for a decade). These provisions require new federal outlays and administrative activity, directly expanding government spending.
The IRS is listed as a covered agency that must support cooperatives, but the bill contains no tax-rate changes, credits, deductions, or revenue provisions.
No provisions address healthcare delivery, insurance, or public coverage.
No provisions relate to firearms or gun regulations.
No provisions address immigration, visas, or border policy.
No provisions address reproductive health or abortion access.
No provisions address military or defense spending.
No provisions address environmental regulation or climate policy.
The bill promotes worker cooperatives as an economic-development tool but does not expand or modify welfare, SNAP, Medicaid, or other entitlement programs.
The bill funds education and outreach about cooperatives, but these are business-development activities, not K-12 public-school funding or school-choice policy.
No provisions address drug enforcement or decriminalization.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
By authorizing new spending and larger lending programs, the bill implicitly accepts additional deficit spending rather than prioritizing debt reduction.
No provisions address LGBTQ legal protections.
No provisions address foreign aid.
No provisions address voting access or election administration.
No provisions address technology regulation or data privacy.

The bill promotes worker-owned cooperatives that give employees majority ownership and control. This directly advances worker economic power and self-management, aligning with the worker-protection end of the labor spectrum even though it does not amend union law.
No provisions address religious exemptions or civil-rights enforcement.
